sections.Profile:
The "3-In-Line" and "Bongo" pinball machines, produced by Bally Manufacturing Co. in the early 1960s, share similar designs with distinct player configurations. ​ "3-In-Line," released in July 1963, is a four-player, electro-mechanical game featuring two flippers, three pop bumpers, two slingshots, five standup targets, and two rollunder lanes. ​ "Bongo," introduced in March 1964, serves as the two-player counterpart to "3-In-Line," maintaining the same playfield layout and features.

- Manufacturer: Bally Manufacturing Co.
- Years made: 1963–1964
- In production: no
- Type: Electro-Mechanical
- Display: Reels
- Players: 4
